name: Battista Guarini
credit: Engraved portrait of Battista Guarini (Wikimedia Commons) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Battista (Giovanni Battista) Guarini (1538–1612) was an Italian poet, courtier and diplomat, born at Ferrara. He studied at Pisa, Padua and Ferrara, taught literature at Ferrara and served the Este dukes as a diplomat and secretary, later holding posts at Turin, Florence and Urbino. A long-running quarrel over his service and over his estates marked much of his life.

His pastoral tragicomedy Il pastor fido (printed 1590) was written in emulation of Tasso's Aminta and became one of the most widely read secular works in Europe for almost two centuries. Its defence, the Compendio della poesia tragicomica, set out his theory of a mixed dramatic form. Guarini also wrote madrigals and other lyrics, and died at Venice in 1612.
